rationale: Found in ⲛⲟⲩ†ⲡⲉ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲛⲃⲟ 'a taste and a ⲛⲃⲟ to what shall be cooked.' Context demands a flavor-noun parallel to ϯⲡⲉ 'taste.' Etymology uncertain — possibly related to ⲛⲡⲣⲉ/ⲛⲟⲩⲡⲉ 'good thing, sweet thing' or a Lyc. flavor-term. Confidence low. Flagged for parallels in subsequent kephalaia.

Object given by fire to whoever touches it. Tentatively read as Lyc. variant of ϩⲙⲟⲩ 'salt' (with vowel insertion ϩⲓⲙⲉ). Salt is a known fire-product (whether by evaporation or as cooking complement) and fits the gustatory-cooking register of this section. Alternative readings include 'a heat' (cf. ⲍⲙⲁⲙ in glossary) — both flag for parallels.

Paired with ⲛⲟⲩϩⲓ̈ⲙⲉ as the second of two qualities given to whoever touches the fire. Etymology obscure — possibly related to a sweetness-root or to ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲁϩ. Functions as a sense-quality complement to salt. Confidence low; flagged.
Singular collective form 'twelve ⲛϩⲱⲁⲓ' = the twelve zodiac-signs. Already attested in glossary as plural ⲛϩⲱⲁⲓⲟⲛ; this confirms the singular/abbreviated form.
